thread.title: Forget the Politics, the Economy Is a Success Story Says Larry Kudlow - TheStreet

author: Katherine Ross
title: Forget the Politics, the Economy Is a Success Story Says Larry Kudlow - TheStreet
text:
Forget the Politics, the Economy Is a Success Story Says Larry Kudlow Larry Kudlow speaks at the New York Economic Club. Sep17,20183:03PMEDT Larry Kudlow speaks at the New York Economic Club.
And the Oscar goes to the economy.
So says Larry Kudlow, who replaced Gary Cohn as one of President Donald Trump's senior economic advisers. Kudlow gave a speech and answered some questions from CNBC's Becky Quick at the New York Economic Club.
"If we lower taxes and remove destructive regulations, we unleash the vast treasure of the" United States economy. There would be "no limit to the number of jobs that we can create," Kudlow said.
"The single biggest story is the economic boom that virtually everyone thought was impossible," Kudlow said. "Give us a chance I ask you." Investors Are Playing a Dangerous Game of Ignoring President Trump
Apple ( AAPL ) CEO Tim Cook "loved our tax reform," said Kudlow. Cook apparently thanked Kudlow and Trump for it.
One of the biggest questions on everyone's mind was the possibility of more tariffs on China . After Kudlow and Quick took their seats, Quick asked about the Chinese tariffs.
"Unfortunately, [the system of free trade after World War 2] has broken down...free trade has to be fair trade...it has to be reciprocal trade," Kudlow said. "The biggest culprit has, in fact, been China. I will say right here...We are willing to negotiate with China. Right here. Anytime."
Kudlow added a caveat, "We are ready to have the discussion at any time so long as it's a serious discussion."
An announcement concerning the possible $200 billion in additional tariffs will be coming "soon." Kudlow added that he doesn't "want to get ahead of the president."
"I don't see any reason to believe, at the present time, that the president's trade reforms are going to damage the economy," Kudlow said. "The person who is trying to fix the system is not the problem, he's the solution." Cramer: Our Financial System is Strong and We Can Benefit From That
Kudlow believes that the economic boom is lost in the news cycles. "In the hubbub of beltway politics, a lot of this is lost. I don't want it to be lost."
Quick moved into a question about the state of politics and how that would affect economic policies if the Democrats were to take control of the House or Senate.
"Given the fact that we've emerged in this economic boom, it would be a shame if policies [were enacted] that unraveled the efforts," Kudlow said. "It would be a great disservice to Americans...don't overturn the good work that's been done."
Kudlow noted that the unemployment rate is down and wages are up. The economy looks good thanks to "more capital investments, more productivity, more jobs, and fatter paychecks."
"It's working!" exclaimed Kudlow, saying that he could talk about the economy for a while. "Everyone benefits from that kind of growth! How can it possibly be bad?"
